abstract: Traditional epidemiologic data suggest that persistent gestational trophoblastic disease (pGTD), may follow, and be derived from, either molar pregnancy, non-molar term pregnancy or first-trimester non-molar miscarriage. We examined a database of cases of possible or probable hydatidiform moles and proven pGTD derived from the Regional Trophoblastic Disease Unit, Charing Cross Hospital, London. There were 424 cases (6%), in whom the initial registered diagnosis was that of PHM or CHM but central histopathological review diagnosed a definite non-molar hydropic abortion (HA). In eight of the 424 (2%), although the histology of the most recent index pregnancy was that of non-molar miscarriage, there was a previous history of pregnancy affected by hydatidiform mole; two of these developed subsequent pGTD. Of a further 86 cases referred for a histopathological opinion prior to registration which demonstrated definite non-molar HA, none developed pGTD (zero of 510 (0%, 95% CI 0-0.7%)). During the same period there were 352 cases with pGTD requiring chemotherapy. In 31 cases, the only known pregnancy was the preceding apparent non-molar HA. However, of these, there were only three cases in whom the preceding histological products of conception had been centrally reviewed and were suggestive of non-molar pregnancy. However, in all three of these cases, the specimens were inadequate for definite exclusion of molar pregnancy. In one case in whom no material was available for review, molecular genetic analysis using restriction fragment length polymorphisms was carried out, and the choriocarcinoma was genetically derived from a previous molar pregnancy rather than the preceding HA. There were therefore no cases identified on the database of the trophoblastic disease unit of pGTD requiring treatment in whom the trophoblastic tumour could be genetically proven to have arisen from the preceding first trimester non-molar HA. We suggest that the risk of pGTD developing from a histologically confirmed non-molar HA is less than 1 in 50,000 and that the majority of pGTD cases previously reported to have been caused by a non-molar miscarriage probably represent disease due to an unrecognised early molar pregnancy.
abstract_ja: 持続性妊娠性絨毛性疾患(pGTD)は、胞状奇胎、非胞状正常分娩、または初期の非胞状流産に続いて生じ、そこから発生すると、従来の疫学データで示唆されている。本研究では、ロンドンのCharing Cross Hospital地域絨毛性疾患ユニットのデータベースを調べた。胞状奇胎の疑い・確定とされ、中央病理診断で明確な非胞状水腫性流産と診断された症例が424例(6%)あった。直近の妊娠の組織所見は非胞状流産であったが、以前に胞状奇胎に罹患した既往がある症例が8例(2%)あり、そのうち2例が続発性pGTDを発症した。登録前に明確な非胞状水腫性流産と判定された86例の追加症例では、いずれもpGTDを発症しなかった(510例中0例、0%、95%信頼区間0-0.7%)。同時期には化学療法を要したpGTD症例が352例あった。31例では、判明している唯一の妊娠が先行する明らかな非胞状流産であった。しかし、これらのうち、先行する妊娠産物が中央で再検討され非胞状妊娠を示唆した症例はわずか3例であった。しかもこの3例はいずれも、胞状奇胎を確実に除外するには検体が不十分であった。組織の検討が不可能であった1例では、制限酵素断片長多型による分子遺伝学的解析が行われ、絨毛癌は先行する水腫性流産ではなく以前の胞状奇胎に由来することが示された。したがって、絨毛性疾患ユニットのデータベースには、先行する初期の非胞状水腫性流産から発生したことを遺伝学的に証明できる、治療を要するpGTDは認められなかった。組織学的に確認された非胞状水腫性流産からpGTDが発生する危険性は5万分の1未満であり、初期の非胞状流産によって生じたと以前報告されたpGTDの大部分は、未認識の初期胞状奇胎による疾患を表している可能性が高いと考える。
